blockers.title: The leftover inventory takes the closing half of G09 v3 and drops the two leftover obligations that same artifact newly introduces on DR-105
blockers.location: summary.leftoverDesign; doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone; obligations (no OBL-R10-AUTHORING, no OBL-R6-AUTHORING); proposedLaterWork
blockers.finding: The artifact this successor exists to incorporate, harness.DR-G09.permissions.preview-scoped.v3 at the pinned d1c7a669, states its own effect on this row in a single field with two halves. The closing half, leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded, holds exactly one entry: OBL-G09-HARNESS-SPEC. The subject takes it and flips that obligation to false. The remaining half, in a field named leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR105, holds eight entries: OBL-FX-AUTHORING, OBL-R10-AUTHORING, OBL-R6-AUTHORING, OBL-FC-C1, and OBL-BLK-1 through OBL-BLK-4. The subject's summary.leftoverDesign holds six. The set difference is exactly OBL-R10-AUTHORING and OBL-R6-AUTHORING — and those two are precisely the ones G09 v3 newly introduced, being absent from the predecessor v2 because G09 v3 did not yet exist. So the two halves of one pinned source were treated differently, and the half that was dropped is the half that adds work to the row. I confirmed the omission is total rather than a naming variation: searching the subject for R-10 outside the DR-105 token, for R-6, for OBL-R10-AUTHORING, for OBL-R6-AUTHORING, and for the phrases race byte-set, process-death and expiry-materialization returns zero of each, against 11, 14, 1 and 1 in G09 v3. The obvious defence, that OBL-FX-AUTHORING already covers them, is foreclosed by the source in terms: 'OBL-FX-AUTHORING remains the D-163 fourteen. This artifact does not widen it. R-10 and R-6 authoring is leftover on DR-105 beyond that fourteen.' G09 v3 repeats the point at each site of use — 'R-10 is not invented as a fifteenth FX class', 'R-6 is not invented as a fifteenth FX class' — and its passProperty holds only once the fourteen FX implementations AND the R-10 byte-set AND the R-6 byte-set exist and are independently pinned. Nor can they be absorbed into OBL-G09-EXECUTION: authoring byte-sets is authoring, which is design work under D-056 Decision clause 5, and the subject applies exactly that reasoning to OBL-FX-AUTHORING two obligations earlier.
blockers.whyItMatters: This artifact is the DR-105 leftover ledger — its stated purpose is to re-measure DR-105 leftover after G09 harness-spec authoring — so the inventory is the deliverable rather than a summary of it. The omission is not silence about something unknown: doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone makes a closed enumeration, 'OBL-FX-AUTHORING, OBL-FC-C1, and OBL-BLK-1..4 remain leftover-design', which reads as exhaustive and is short by two against the artifact it pins one field away. The corpus pattern is that a D-000 recording adopts the join as the row's ledger, exactly as D-163 recorded v2, so a recording of v3 would inscribe an inventory missing two obligations. Nothing downstream recovers them, because proposedLaterWork also plans only 'the fourteen FX fixture implementations' while G09 v3's own proposedLaterWork carries a separate item for the R-10 and R-6 byte-sets.
blockers.whatItDoesNotDo: Stated so the severity is not read as wider than it is. This does not change the DR-105 token, which is OPEN live and stays OPEN. It does not make the row D-056-eligible — gates 2 and 3 fail on the six retained obligations alone, and G09 v3 independently records gates2and3HoldForDR105 as false. It does not touch required-now, which is 26 of 26 live. The error understates remaining leftover; it does not overstate progress on any gate.
blockers.whatWouldRepairIt: Carry the two obligations the source names — OBL-R10-AUTHORING and OBL-R6-AUTHORING, leftoverDesign true, not folded into OBL-FX-AUTHORING — into obligations and summary.leftoverDesign, extend the doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone enumeration, and add the byte-set authoring item to proposedLaterWork. The classification requires no judgment: G09 v3 supplies it verbatim.
blockers.notAssertedByThisFinding: I do not author the R-10 or R-6 bytes, propose their content, invent an OBL numbering beyond the two identifiers G09 v3 already names, or assert that G09 v3's classification of them is correct. The finding is only that the subject silently departs from the source it relies on.

advisories.title: recordedInputs was carried forward unrefreshed while head was updated, leaving two different HEAD values and one stale digest in a digest-pinning artifact
advisories.detail: v3 updated top-level head from 8fd376d6 to 5d5d778 but left recordedInputs byte-identical to v2's, so the artifact now carries head 5d5d778 alongside recordedInputs.HEAD 8fd376d6, and a COORD digest that no longer reproduces. This is not a false claim: recordedInputs is internally coherent as a D-162 snapshot, its HEAD equals its own 'D-162 commit' value, and that commit is exactly where the cited COORD blob lives. The remeasurementClause then pre-authorizes append-only COORD drift as PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT, and I verified the drift really is pure append rather than taking the clause on trust. So it is advisory, not a finding. The residue is that a reader checking the twelve pinned digests hits one mismatch with no annotation, and must reconstruct the append-only proof before knowing whether it matters. I raised nothing on this block against v2 and accepted v2 at 0/0; the only new fact at v3 is that one HEAD field moved and its neighbour did not, which is worth a note and not an escalation. A dated marker on recordedInputs, or a line recording that COORD has since advanced append-only to 38297e5b, would close it.

independence.priorParticipation: Substantial, and it cuts directly at this finding. I reviewed and accepted permission-leftover-join.v2 at 0/0/0, and I am the author of CLAUDE-G09H-V2-SF1, the finding against the G09 harness v2 that required R-10 and R-6 to be carried in its inventory and passProperty — G09 v3 names that finding by ID as what it lands. So the identifiers whose absence I now report as a blocker exist in the corpus because of a finding of mine, and I had them in mind before I opened this subject. Two guards. First, the finding does not rest on my prior view: G09 v3's own bytes classify R-10 and R-6 as leftover-design remaining on DR-105 and expressly forbid folding them into OBL-FX-AUTHORING, so the standard applied is the source artifact's, not mine, and it would land for a reviewer who had never seen my G09 review. Second, I checked my prior acceptance for goalpost-moving: v2 could not have carried these identifiers, since G09 v3 did not exist when v2 was written, so accepting v2 at 0/0 and rejecting v3 here is not an inconsistency. What I could not fully neutralize is that noticing the gap was easy for me and would be harder for a reviewer without that history; I record it so the weight given to the finding can account for its origin.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Fifteen attacks run, one landed. Custody holds: subject 1862463f at 0444, 18651 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; live DR-105 token OPEN; file 08 live digest equals the subject's pin; v2 remains exactly 68ea10e0 as the dispatch requires. Eleven of twelve cited digests reproduce. The twelfth is COORD, and rather than accept the subject's remeasurementClause I tested it: the cited digest is exactly the COORD blob at commit 8fd376d6, which is also recordedInputs' own HEAD and D-162 commit, and drift from there to HEAD is 155 insertions with 0 deletions and a byte-identical prefix — pure append, with every file the clause requires unmoved. PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT holds on its own terms. Every dispatch prohibition is refuted by measurement. All nine SATISFIED/QUALIFIED occurrences were walked with field paths and each is a refusal or quoted standing; the single D9 mention, the single §7.1 mention and both implementation-path mentions all sit inside the doesNot list as refusals; fcC1Recorded and newRowProposed are both false. The successor delta was measured against v2 key by key rather than read from v3's account of itself: exactly one obligation changes, OBL-G09-HARNESS-SPEC, and the flip is correct — the named identifier is genuinely authored at a pinned artifact whose independent verdict I confirmed reads ACCEPT, the obligation is retained rather than deleted, the residue routes to OBL-G09-EXECUTION as qualification, and D-167 is refused in three places. Internal bookkeeping is sound: 16 obligations, 16 summary entries, no orphan or duplicate either direction, and the six leftoverDesign flags match summary.leftoverDesign exactly. The blocker is asymmetric extraction from the one source this successor exists to incorporate. G09 v3 states its effect on this row in one field with two halves. The subject takes the closing half — one obligation — and drops two of the eight in the remaining half. The set difference is exactly OBL-R10-AUTHORING and OBL-R6-AUTHORING, which are precisely the two that artifact newly introduced and that v2 could not have carried. The omission is total: R-10 outside the DR-105 token, R-6, both OBL identifiers, and the phrases race byte-set, process-death and expiry-materialization all return zero in the subject against 11, 14, 1 and 1 in G09 v3. The defence that OBL-FX-AUTHORING covers them is foreclosed by the source verbatim — it 'remains the D-163 fourteen', is not widened, and R-10 and R-6 are 'leftover on DR-105 beyond that fourteen' — and they cannot ride OBL-G09-EXECUTION because authoring byte-sets is design work under D-056 clause 5, which is the very reasoning the subject applies to OBL-FX-AUTHORING two obligations earlier. It matters because this artifact is the row's ledger, its doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone makes a closed enumeration that is short by two, the corpus pattern is for a D-000 recording to adopt the join as the ledger exactly as D-163 adopted v2, and proposedLaterWork plans only the fourteen so nothing downstream recovers them. The limits are stated in the finding: the token stays OPEN, gates 2 and 3 fail on the retained six alone, required-now is untouched, and the error understates remaining work rather than overstating progress. Repair needs no judgment — G09 v3 supplies the classification verbatim. Two advisories: recordedInputs was carried forward unrefreshed while head was updated, leaving two HEAD values and one unannotated stale digest, which the remeasurementClause defuses and which I did not raise against v2; and live file 08 still calls the G09 harness 'not authored' at both the DR-G09 row and condition 4, which is now stale but is the register's to fix, not this artifact's. One disclosure the coordinator should weigh: I am the author of the G09-harness finding that put R-10 and R-6 into the corpus, so I came to this subject already holding those identifiers. The finding does not rest on that — it applies G09 v3's own classification from G09 v3's own bytes — but noticing the gap was easier for me than it would be for a reviewer without that history. I also declined to read the v2 Codex verdict, which exists, so I cannot say whether it raised findings v3 should have dispositioned; the Claude side owed none, since my v2 verdict was ACCEPT 0/0/0.
